correctness.rationale: The Gamma Laplace law and inverse-moment scale limit give exactly the stated F_k(a). Its integrand has one sign switch at t=8(k-1); e^{8(k-1)a}F_k(a) has strictly negative derivative. For 2<k<=5/2 the zero-damping integral diverges positively, and high damping yields a negative Watson-lemma asymptotic, forcing one simple root. A bounded-kernel fitted-parameter V-statistic expansion gives an L2 influence function because k>2. At the zero, its fitted-scale derivative is (a/lambda*) F_k'(a), nonzero, and the singular 1/x score prevents cancellation of the bounded first projection; hence a positive finite CLT variance and nonconsistent two-sided testing. Actual verify.py completed 33 numerical assertions, supplementary only. Risks: no independent checking and the CLT uses fixed a, shape, scale.

value.rationale: The location and uniqueness of a complete signed-test inconsistency curve for a natural continuum of Gamma shape alternatives expose a real boundary of using an integrated signed discrepancy; the Gamma shape range is structurally pinned by the heavy-tail integrability of the Laplace integrand and CLT integrability of the inverse-moment fitting score. The result informs safe tuning interpretation, although the blind weights are outside the simulation grid and practical finite-n performance is not claimed.
